propositions: add_comment returns raw ACLI batch mutation envelope {results, totalCount, successCount} instead of normalizing to comment resource {id, ...} at the transport boundary
gap between declared return type (comment resource) and actual return (batch envelope) allows callers like _record_comment_id to read results[].id (work item key) mistaking it for comment id
sibling operations (get_comments, get_issue, create_issue) normalize or verify payloads before returning; add_comment skips this idiom and exposes callers to semantic-shape hazard
acli.update_issue in acli.py has same raw-passthrough pattern for workitem edit --json but currently poses no consumer hazard since its only caller treats return opaquely
normalizer must distinguish resource-shaped dicts (pass through) from batch envelopes (wrap with id:None, preserve envelope under acli_envelope key) to prevent results[].id field trap
